newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australian dlr content to hold under US$0.79.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australian dlr content to hold under US$0.79.

text.p: The Australian dollar spent a quiet afternoon session settling above the morning's lows but contained under US$0.7900 as continuing talk of a rate cut this week saw the market hold a cautious tone.
Trading was subdued as a result of a lack of data and the U.S. market being closed, with even the weekend tensions in Iraq failing to stir markets much.
By 4.45 p.m. the Australian dollar was at US$0.7896/01, down from an early US$0.7904/09, and almost level with Friday's local US$0.7895/00 close.
Aginst the yen, the AUD had recovered from a morning slip below 86 yen by the close, helped by a move in the U.S. dollar back over 109 yen.
In trade weighted terms, the AUD closed steady at 57.9.
The AUD had slipped to a low of US$0.7880 in morning trade as Friday's speculation of a local rate cut this week continued to weigh on the unit.

While most do not expect a cut to follow Tuesday's Reserve Bank Board meeting, traders were not willing to bet against it after many were caught out when the cash rate was lowered to 7.00 percent on July 31.

Reuters surveyed 35 economists ahead of the RBA board meeting this week and only one said a September rate change was possible. While a clear majority favoured a cut as the next move in rates, they did not expect it until the fourth quarter, with November the most favoured time.
The RBA board meets on Tuesday, and the earliest it could announce a change policy would be Wednesday, when it releases its dealing intentions at 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT Tuesday).
With the rate cut talk providing an effective cap, the absence of any dual currency samurai issues, one of the main supports of the AUD recently, allowed the dollar to soften.

Traders said an easing in rates would narrow the interest differential to both Japan and the U.S., and would lessen the attractiveness of further samurai issues, and was thus keeping the market cautious.

In contrast to its effect on the AUD, the rate speculation is boosting local capital markets. With U.S. Treasuries beginning to factor in a near term Fed Reserve tightening, the spread between local and U.S. bonds narrowed to a two year low of 115 basis points in trading on Monday.
In other news today, Treasury Secretary Ted Evans painted a fairly upbeat picture of the economy in a speech in Sydney.

Evans said that despite the planned reduction in the budget deficit, equivalent to 1.5 percent of GDP over the next two years, Australia would continue "to enjoy quite robust growth in the short term."
Evans also said the outlook for wages, a key determinant of monetary policy settings, was uncertain, adding that wages growth needed to be underpinned by productivity imporvements.

July retail trade data on Tuesday is expected to show only a 0.5 percent rise, confirming the recent sluggishness of the economy. A weak number would heighten speculation of a rate cut, traders said. -- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
